name: Demolition & environmental remediation
notes: Public, authoritative per-unit prices for building demolition, hazardous-material abatement, UST removal and soil remediation were not retrievable in this session (search budget exhausted; consumer cost sites partially blocked). Values are therefore mostly derived, bounded by Fixr consumer guides (low confidence, residential) and DOT pavement-removal bid prices. Treat these as allowances pending a Phase I/II ESA and a hazardous-materials survey.

items.name: Building demolition, complete (structure + slab/foundations, haul & disposal; excl. abatement)

cost.method: Fixr residential house demolition $5-$10/SF on average, ~$3/SF for older homes without foundations and up to ~$12/SF with full basements (e1). Commercial buildings benefit from scale (1-2 story wood/steel/masonry: ~$4-$8/SF) but concrete frames, multi-story and urban sites with shoring/dust control run $10-$15+/SF. Mid $8/SF for a typical 1-2 story commercial building incl. slab and footing removal and landfill fees, net of minimal salvage.

items.notes: Per gross SF demolished. Add asbestos/lead abatement, UST removal and utility disconnects separately. High-rise/implosion work is outside this range.

items.name: Interior demolition / selective strip-out (to shell; excl. abatement)

cost.method: Derived. Selective demolition is labor-intensive and protects remaining structure; for adaptive reuse and tenant-improvement strip-outs a typical range is ~40-80% of complete building demolition cost per SF (building-demolition mid $8) for a light strip of partitions/ceilings/finishes ($3-$5), rising to $8-$12 when MEP systems, floors and stairs are removed in occupied or multi-story buildings. Mid $6.

items.notes: Adaptive reuse / renovation projects (office-to-resi, retail repositioning, hotel PIPs).

items.name: Pavement / slab removal & disposal (asphalt or concrete)

cost.method: FDOT removal of existing concrete $34.32/SY (192 contracts, 436,447 SY, e4); ArDOT removal & disposal of concrete pavement $9.70/SY (7,492 SY) and removal of existing PCC pavement $43.35/SY (e5). Highway concrete is thick and reinforced; private parking-lot asphalt removal is far cheaper. Mid $20 = between the ArDOT and FDOT weighted averages; low = asphalt lots in volume; high = thick reinforced concrete.

items.notes: Redevelopment of existing parking lots / pads. Recycled base can sometimes be reused on site.

items.name: Asbestos abatement (ACM removal under containment, disposal, clearance air testing) - per SF of affected material

cost.method: Fixr: licensed removal often '$5 to $20 per sq.ft.' (e2, 2022 residential), with easy materials (popcorn ceilings) at $3-$7/SF. Commercial abatement of floor tile/mastic and non-friable material in volume runs low ($4-$6/SF); friable pipe/fireproofing in containment at the high end. Mid $9 reflects a mix weighted to non-friable floor/ceiling materials.

items.notes: Quantity from the pre-demolition asbestos survey (required by NESHAP before demolition/renovation). If unknown for pre-1981 buildings, many owners carry $2-$5 per building SF as an allowance.

items.name: Lead-based paint abatement (stabilization/removal) - per SF of painted surface treated

cost.method: Fixr: encapsulation $1-$4/SF, enclosure $6-$12/SF, removal $8-$17/SF (e3, Jan 2025). Mid $8 assumes a mix of encapsulation and component removal typical of housing rehab; low = mostly encapsulation; high = full removal.

items.notes: Pre-1978 housing (HUD Lead Safe Housing Rule applies to federally assisted rehab). Interim controls are cheaper than abatement.

items.name: Contaminated soil remediation - excavate, transport & dispose (non-hazardous / petroleum), incl. backfill

cost.method: Derived. Non-hazardous petroleum-impacted soil: excavation and loading ~$8-$15/CY (cf. DOT excavation $6.81-$18.51/CY in site-work.json#e3/#e5), transport and Subtitle D landfill disposal ~$30-$70 per ton x ~1.5 tons/CY = $45-$105/CY, confirmation sampling and clean backfill ~$10-$30/CY (import-fill) -> $63-$150; mid $110. High $250 covers longer hauls, special-waste profiling and characteristic (non-RCRA-listed) soils; RCRA hazardous soil can exceed $400/CY and is outside this range.

items.notes: Volume comes from a Phase II ESA. Brownfield grants/state cleanup programs may offset cost. In-situ treatment and vapor mitigation are separate.

items.name: Underground storage tank removal & closure (one tank ≤12,000 gal, incl. product/sludge removal, closure sampling; excl. contaminated soil)

cost.method: Derived. Typical scope: permit and fire-marshal oversight, pumping residual product/sludge ($1k-$4k), excavation and tank cleaning/cutting and disposal ($4k-$12k), piping and dispenser removal, closure soil/groundwater sampling and report ($2k-$6k), and clean backfill/compaction ($1k-$5k) -> $8k-$27k per tank; mid $15k. High $30k = larger/fiberglass tanks or difficult urban access. Contaminated soil and groundwater work are carried in soil-remediation.

items.notes: Former gas stations, fleet yards, older commercial properties with heating-oil tanks. Multiple tanks in one excavation get economies of scale (~20-30% less per additional tank).
